clue.text: Forge common name, then unknown

parts.note: Smith is the most common surname in Britain
Y is an algebraic unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: Someone forges a common name for themselves, and the rest is a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forge' reads as a verb meaning fake, but it is the noun: a blacksmith's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's workshop, where iron is heated and hammered, is called by both names.

clue.text: Reformed teenager becoming calming influence?

indicators.note: a reformed character has been remade, so the letters of the next word are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tearaway youth has turned over a new leaf and now soothes everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' rearranges TEENAGER; the question mark marks the definition as loose, since the drink is thought to be soothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The pale Chinese brew is widely drunk as a soothing, relaxing beverage.

clue.text: Play match without man, stand-in

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the match word wraps around the rest

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
he is a pronoun standing for a man
a temp is a temporary worker standing in for someone

explanation.surface: A team plays a game without one player, using a substitute instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. A Test match is an international cricket fixture, and a temp is a temporary office worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late drama of Prospero's island is one of his best-known stage works.

clue.text: Ready for sport

definitions.meaning: willing, up for it, as in being prepared to have a go
a match or contest, as in a round of cards or football

explanation.surface: Someone is set to play a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A willing person is said to be up for anything, and a match of football or tennis is a contest of this kind.

clue.text: Heart of the necropolis, perhaps?

parts.note: a city of the departed has a middle point that belongs to the departed, read as a phrase for an exact middle

explanation.surface: Asking what lies at the very middle of an ancient cemetery.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means an exact middle point, but read literally it is the centre of a city of corpses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means exactly in the middle, punning on a burial city whose inhabitants are deceased.

clue.text: Flog in prison quarters, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, so we need something that sounds alike

parts.note: an inmate's room in jail is a cell

explanation.surface: Selling contraband from a jail cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' looks like whipping, but it is slang for selling.
explanation.definitionFit: Flog is informal British slang for offering goods for money.

clue.text: God embraced by peevish nuns

indicators.note: the deity is held inside the words that follow, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A god is hugged by irritable nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindu preserver deity forms a trinity with Brahma and Shiva.

clue.text: But sun is cheap, they say, for the animal

indicators.note: they say indicates that the following words are spoken and sound like the answer

parts.note: flip each to its opposite: not sun but rain, not cheap but dear

explanation.surface: Someone comparing sunshine with costs, oddly naming an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually, the pieces are opposites: the contrary of 'sun' is RAIN and of 'cheap' is DEAR. Spoken, 'rain dear' gives the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arctic deer, used to pull sledges, is the creature meant.

clue.text: Main drug injected into horse, producing mad animal?

indicators.note: injected puts one thing inside another, here inside the horse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
arch as an adjective means chief or principal
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Doping a horse with a powerful drug makes it go wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' means chief, giving ARCH. The definition refers to the proverb 'mad as a March hare', and the creature in Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'mad as a March hare' comes from the wild behaviour of the creatures in the spring breeding season.

clue.text: One left in river, one thrown out of country

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the river name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A person left behind on a riverbank while another is banished.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A banished person is sent away from their homeland.

clue.text: Support Scrabble letters

indicators.note: scrabble as a verb means scramble, so the following word's letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Tiles in the board game are used to prop something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrabble' looks like the board game but tells us to scramble LETTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame on legs is used as a stand to hold up a tabletop.

clue.text: Police backing clue not entirely the main source of intelligence?

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the police word is read in reverse

parts.note: Plod is British slang for the police, from Mr Plod in Enid Blyton

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the clue word is lost

parts.note: a hint is a clue

explanation.surface: Police going back over a partial clue in search of the chief source of information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the sea, as in the Spanish Main, and the definition plays on spies: a clever sea creature. PLOD (British slang for police) is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly intelligent marine mammal is a brainy creature of the ocean.

clue.text: Elusive giant, one unseen to this day

indicators.note: unseen says a piece is gone from view, so it is taken out

parts.note: the yeti is the elusive abominable snowman of the Himalayas
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Nobody has ever spotted the mysterious beast so far.
explanation.definitionFit: Still, until now, as in 'not finished so far'.

clue.text: Ineffective character

definitions.meaning: useless, amateurish or trivial, as in a toy-like organisation
a cartoon figure, Disney's famous creation

explanation.surface: Describing a useless person.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's cartoon rodent lends his name as slang for something amateurish and second-rate.

clue.text: Possible Russian battlefield where Nazi pig breaks record

indicators.note: breaks says one piece splits another apart and sits inside it

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a recording
Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A Nazi and a swine smash a record on a Russian field of war.
explanation.walkthrough: Russians are famed chess players, so their 'battlefield' is the game's board.
explanation.definitionFit: The chequered square on which chess, a war game Russians dominate, is fought.

clue.text: Fish-my fish, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the words are spoken and sound like the answer

parts.note: my refers to the setter, Mudd, and a kipper is a smoked fish: Mudd's kipper

explanation.surface: Someone calls their own fish a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the setter speaking: this crossword is by Mudd, so 'my fish' is Mudd's kipper.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphibious goby that hops over tidal flats using its fins.

clue.text: Fish has to pass over ice

definitions.meaning: a flat cartilaginous sea creature related to rays
to glide across a frozen surface on blades

explanation.surface: A fish glides across a frozen pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ray is a sea creature, and to glide on blades across a rink is the verb.

clue.text: Black Rod's shortened headgear

parts.note: sombre means dark or gloomy

indicators.note: shortened means the name is cut back, losing its final letter

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A parliamentary official known as Black Rod wears a hat that is too short.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Rod is a ceremonial officer of the UK House of Lords; the surface reads it as one title, but the two words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed Mexican hat is a type of headwear.

clue.text: Put away 'otness

indicators.note: the apostrophe marks the dropped first letter, as in a Cockney accent

parts.note: the printed word is warmth with its opening letter dropped, Cockney style

explanation.surface: Dismissing the warmth, in a dropped-aitch accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe shows a dropped H, as in Cockney speech: 'otness is HEAT without its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is to consume it.

clue.text: River runs past daughter he painted

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A river flows past a girl whom an artist painted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, and R for runs is a cricket scoring abbreviation. 'past' just places URE and R after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was the German Renaissance artist famed for engravings and paintings.

clue.text: Journalist's 'written line to plug Conservatives with indication of sleaze

indicators.note: to plug puts the pieces into a gap inside the Conservatives word

parts.note: the right is the conservative wing in politics
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter writes up a scandal about Tory politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written' is just a link here; the journalist is ED, an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp of this colour traditionally marks a brothel district.

clue.text: Little pale, say, as rare meat

parts.note: minute means very small

indicators.note: say tells us a word is spoken and sounds like another

parts.note: a pale is a fence post, the same as a stake

explanation.surface: Something tiny and pallid, likened to undercooked beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pale' looks like an adjective but is the noun: a fence post.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin cut of beef cooked very quickly, so it stays bloody inside.

clue.text: Settle for some honest lecturing

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Accepting a bit of truthful teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuggle down comfortably into a position.

clue.text: Failure from the left and right

indicators.note: the word reads identically whichever direction it is taken in

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A flop seen from both political sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome, the same read from the left or right.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud is something that does not work, like a shell that does not explode.

clue.text: Point to school shown up after a couple of low grades

indicators.note: after puts the school piece behind the grades

parts.note: D and E are poor exam grades

indicators.note: shown up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Eton is a famous English private school

explanation.surface: Indicating a school embarrassed by its poor exam marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' reverses ETON, the English public school, in this down clue; D and E are low exam grades.
explanation.definitionFit: To signify or indicate something.

clue.text: King is meeting German king for dinner

parts.note: R is short for rex, king
Otto was the name of several German kings and emperors

explanation.surface: Two monarchs meet for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The creamy Italian rice dish is served as a main meal.

clue.text: Wrong pace, going the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the pace word is read backwards

parts.note: a trot is a running pace

explanation.surface: An error in tempo, heading the wrong direction.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a civil wrong for which damages can be sought.

clue.text: Title fitting in chapter one, then write on

indicators.note: in places the fitting word inside the chapter-and-one pair

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
apt means suitable
taken as written

explanation.surface: Picking the right heading for chapter one, then continuing to write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chapter one' gives C and I as separate abbreviations; 'then write' is only a link before the final piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Words placed under a picture to describe it serve as a heading.

clue.text: Hit copper very powerfully

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
ff, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: A police officer strikes hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, CU.
explanation.definitionFit: A light blow with the open hand.

clue.text: Leader taking the direct line?

definitions.meaning: one who governs, such as a monarch
a measuring stick used for drawing straight lines

explanation.surface: A boss who follows the straight path.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch governs, and a measuring stick draws straight lines.

clue.text: Bullet finding intended target, perhaps, during battle

indicators.note: during places one piece within the span of the other

parts.note: a riot is a violent disturbance or fight
flesh is what a bullet is aimed at, for example

explanation.surface: A bullet hits its mark in the middle of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bullet' alone is the definition; 'perhaps' warns that the target is defined by example, since what a gunman aims at is a body.
explanation.definitionFit: A single discharge from a long gun is a firing.
